Medical Decision Calculator

Source: R/decisioncalculator.h.R
decisioncalculator.Rd

Medical Decision Calculator for diagnostic test evaluation when you have the four key counts: True Positives (TP), False Positives (FP), True Negatives (TN), and False Negatives (FN). Calculates comprehensive diagnostic performance metrics including sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, likelihood ratios, and post-test probabilities. Supports confidence interval estimation and Fagan nomogram visualization for educational interpretation. Presets and examples are illustrative only and are not clinical guides.

Usage

decisioncalculator(
  TP = 90,
  TN = 80,
  FP = 30,
  FN = 20,
  pp = FALSE,
  pprob = 0.3,
  fnote = FALSE,
  ci = FALSE,
  fagan = FALSE,
  faganColors = "jamovi",
  showWelcome = FALSE,
  showSummary = FALSE,
  showAbout = FALSE,
  showGlossary = FALSE,
  multiplecuts = FALSE,
  cutoff1 = "Higher sensitivity example",
  tp1 = 100,
  fp1 = 40,
  tn1 = 70,
  fn1 = 10,
  cutoff2 = "Higher specificity example",
  tp2 = 80,
  fp2 = 15,
  tn2 = 95,
  fn2 = 30,
  showWorkload = FALSE,
  workloadPopulationSize = 1000,
  prevalenceScenarios = "0.0001,0.001,0.01",
  analysisUnit = "patient"
)

Arguments

TP

True-positive frequency relative to the stated reference standard.

TN

True-negative frequency relative to the stated reference standard.

FP

False-positive frequency relative to the stated reference standard.

FN

False-negative frequency relative to the stated reference standard.

pp

Boolean selection whether to use known population prevalence for prevalence-dependent predictive measures.

pprob

Prior probability (disease prevalence in the community). Requires a value strictly between 0 and 1, default 0.300.

fnote

Boolean selection whether to show detailed explanatory footnotes.

ci

Boolean selection whether to calculate 95 percent confidence intervals.

fagan

Boolean selection whether to generate a Fagan nomogram plot.

faganColors

Colors of the Fagan nomogram's lines: "jamovi" follows the global palette, "classic" draws the positive-result line red and the negative-result line blue.

showWelcome

Boolean selection whether to show welcome message.

showSummary

Boolean selection whether to show plain-language summary of results.

showAbout

Boolean selection whether to show about and assumptions panels.

showGlossary

Boolean selection whether to show clinical glossary.

multiplecuts

Boolean selection whether to evaluate multiple cut-off scenarios.

cutoff1

Name identifier for cut-off scenario 1.

tp1

True-positive frequency for illustrative scenario 1.

fp1

False-positive frequency for illustrative scenario 1.

tn1

True-negative frequency for illustrative scenario 1.

fn1

False-negative frequency for illustrative scenario 1.

cutoff2

Name identifier for cut-off scenario 2.

tp2

True-positive frequency for illustrative scenario 2.

fp2

False-positive frequency for illustrative scenario 2.

tn2

True-negative frequency for illustrative scenario 2.

fn2

False-negative frequency for illustrative scenario 2.

showWorkload

Boolean selection whether to show the observed and projected workload table.

workloadPopulationSize

Population size used for the projected workload rows.

prevalenceScenarios

Comma-separated proportions between 0 and 1 (at most 100) at which workload is projected.

analysisUnit

Label for the unit each count represents, shown in the workload table.

Value

A results object containing:

results$noticesa preformatted
results$welcomea html
results$summarya html
results$abouta html
results$assumptionsa html
results$glossarya html
results$cTablea table
results$nTablea table
results$ratioTablea table
results$advancedMetricsTablea table
results$epirTable_ratioa table
results$epirTable_numbera table
results$faganSummaryPlain-language reading of the Fagan nomogram: the pre-test probability, the likelihood ratios, and where a positive or a negative result moves the probability of disease.
results$plot1an image
results$multipleCutoffTablea table
results$screeningWorkloada table

Tables can be converted to data frames with asDF or as.data.frame. For example:

results$cTable$asDF

as.data.frame(results$cTable)

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Illustrative examples only; these are not clinical guides.
result1 <- decisioncalculator(
  TP = 90, FN = 20, TN = 80, FP = 30
)

result2 <- decisioncalculator(
  TP = 90, FN = 20, TN = 80, FP = 30,
  ci = TRUE, pp = TRUE, pprob = 0.15, fagan = TRUE
)
} # }
